pin_and_eviction_contract.raii_guard: PageGuard (buffer.rs:103-107); pin_count incremented at buffer.rs:369/398/409, decremented in Drop (buffer.rs:872-879)
pin_and_eviction_contract.holders_audited: heap append (append.rs:154-249), heap read (mutation/read.rs), heap scan (page_heap/scan.rs:253-259), btree insert/delete/lookup/cursor (index/mutate/insert.rs:57-99, index/lookup.rs:44) — all pin ONE page at a time and drop before the next; no struct stores PageGuard outside buffer.rs; no per-column writer exists (web store writes whole-row JSON blobs)
pin_and_eviction_contract.key_finding_not_a_pin_leak: ensure_capacity is ONLY ever called with durable_lsn=Lsn::ZERO — buffer.rs:363 (allocate) and buffer.rs:404 (pin cold path). evict_one skips every dirty frame whose page_lsn > durable_lsn (buffer.rs:634) and flush_frame_if_durable refuses to flush them (buffer.rs:772-779). Therefore ALL DIRTY FRAMES ARE PERMANENTLY UNEVICTABLE from the allocate/pin path regardless of actual WAL durability. The error text ('no unpinned frame') is misleading: exhaustion is by dirty frames, not pinned frames.
pin_and_eviction_contract.only_relief_valves: explicit Database::checkpoint() (engine/maintenance.rs:203-241 flush_dirty_batches with real durable LSN). jain-web calls it ONLY at shutdown (lifecycle.rs:139), hourly GC sweep (main.rs:214-230, DEFAULT_GC_INTERVAL_SECS=3600, lifecycle.rs:217), and backup. No engine-internal auto-checkpoint exists.
pin_and_eviction_contract.page_reuse_debt_confirmed: page ids are append-only monotonic (buffer.rs:150 next_page_id=page_count+1, buffer.rs:364 fetch_add); reusable pages are produced only by vacuum (page_heap/directory/vacuum.rs:124-139) and Store::vacuum (feat-web store/storage.rs:91-93) has no runtime callers

threshold_arithmetic.budget: pool = 16 MiB / 16 KiB = 1024 frames; because dirty frames are unevictable (buffer.rs:634 @ durable_lsn=ZERO) and no checkpoint runs during the E2E window (first GC sweep at t+3600 s), the process has a hard lifetime budget of ~1024 DISTINCT DIRTIED PAGES (~16 MiB of heap+undo+index page dirtying) from container start until the first checkpoint
column_proportional_writers: profile_json ~= 95-105 B/column: 130 cols ~= 13 KB (~1 page/write), 72 cols ~= 7 KB (<1/2 page)

at predict-time profiling both files (train 1000x130 + scoring 999x130) are re-profiled: 2x set_file_profile + set_session_profile (2-file profile + schema_diff ~= 26-30 KB) + profile.complete event payload duplicating it
every UPDATE also writes a full before-image undo cell (append_update_version) => byte volume x2

MVCC multiplier: after initial profiling, sessions.profile_json rides in the sessions row; EVERY subsequent state transition (transition_with_event/set_state, ~12-15 per run) appends a complete new row version + full before-image => ~2-4 fresh 16 KiB pages per transition at 130 cols vs ~1-2 at 72 cols

training progress: every feat-core progress event + reasoning.note is persisted (runner/sink.rs:80-99); hundreds to low-thousands of event INSERTs/run, each dirtying heap+undo+PK-btree pages; payload sizes and event counts grow with feature count (phases 1-6 iterate over features)
threshold_arithmetic.why_130_fails_72_passes: cumulative distinct dirtied pages over (training run + predict upload + re-profiling) crosses the 1024-frame cliff for the 130-col Allstate run and stays under it for the 72-col fixture; the predict-time double-profile burst (~40-80 fresh pages at 130 cols, roughly half at 72) is the straw. The relationship is capacity-proportional in total bytes written since boot, dominated by column-proportional JSON blobs and their MVCC/undo copies — matching the observed 'more columns -> more pages' signature. Exact page counts need runtime counters (BufferPoolStats.resident_pages/evictions) — see limitations
threshold_arithmetic.sagemaker_control: /invocations path does not write session events/profiles to the web redline store, so it passes both fixtures
threshold_arithmetic.jain_web_max_data_bytes_irrelevant: JAIN_WEB_MAX_DATA_BYTES=2147483648 only feeds GC prune sizing (lifecycle.rs:172-187); the binding cap is the 16 MiB buffer pool

wedge_mechanism.stuck_in_profiling: upload_files error path restores previous state with `let _ = state.store.set_state(&id, previous_state)` (uploads.rs:131-139) — that UPDATE itself needs a heap append -> fails against the saturated pool and is silently swallowed; every later transition fails the same way, so the session is pinned at 'profiling' until restart (lifecycle reconcile runs only at boot, lifecycle.rs:41-72)
wedge_mechanism.cpu_and_api_hang: no literal unbounded loop exists at the error site (ensure_capacity errors out; SQL autocommit retry excludes CorruptPage — exec/mod.rs:1556-1565). The sustained ~100% CPU + API-wide unresponsiveness is explained by: (a) EVERY cold pin/allocate across all requests serializes on the single Inner::eviction mutex (buffer.rs:65, 593-596) and runs an O(2x1024) sweep including an all_frames() Vec+Arc-clone of the whole pool (buffer.rs:725-738) with zero backoff — at/near saturation nearly every session poll, WS replay and event write does this; the few remaining clean frames thrash (evict -> immediately reloaded); (b) conflict-class errors (SerializationFailure/WriteConflict/LockTimeout) between concurrent event writers on the shared sessions row enter the autocommit retry loop: up to 4096 immediate retries with only std::thread::yield_now() (sql/src/exec/mod.rs:1406, 1527-1539); (c) the 8-connection pool (redline.rs:9) queues behind (a)+(b), so all handlers (reads included, they share the pool) stall
wedge_mechanism.gc_relief_fragile: even the hourly relief is ordering-fragile: run_gc_sweep does prune_storage + trim_session_events BEFORE store.checkpoint() (lifecycle.rs:207-222); if any of those needs a write against the saturated pool it errors and the checkpoint is skipped
wedge_mechanism.confidence: stuck-state mechanism: high (direct code path). CPU/hang attribution: medium — consistent with all code paths found, but a stack sample (e.g. perf top / gdb thread apply all bt on a wedged container) is required to close it definitively

adjacent_risk_noted: any single row whose encoded cell exceeds 16316 B (e.g. sessions row carrying a 2-file wide-column profile_json) hits Error::RecordTooLarge (append.rs:251-260) — no overflow/TOAST mechanism exists in the SQL layer; wide datasets are also near this cliff independent of the buffer pool

fix_proposals_ranked.proposal: give BufferPool access to the real WAL durable LSN (e.g. Arc<AtomicU64> installed by the engine after WAL init at engine/recovery.rs:65-71) and use it instead of Lsn::ZERO at buffer.rs:363 and buffer.rs:404, so ensure_capacity/evict_one can flush-and-evict dirty pages whose LSN is durable (with Strict commit durability nearly all dirty pages become flushable immediately). Pool then self-heals under write pressure.

auto-checkpoint watermark: when dirty/resident crosses e.g. 50% of capacity, run flush_dirty_batches with the current durable LSN (background thread or inline in allocate path) instead of relying solely on caller checkpoints.

decouple checkpointing from GC: short-interval store.checkpoint() (30-60 s or every N events) in its own tokio task, AND reorder/guard run_gc_sweep so checkpoint() runs first (or in a finally) so failing prunes can't skip the relief valve.
raise memory.cache_bytes for the web store open (e.g. 256 MiB => 16384 frames) — moves the cliff, does not remove it.

split the error into 'all frames pinned' vs 'dirty pages exceed durable horizon'; add bounded backoff + one forced flush attempt before failing; surface BufferPoolStats in the web /api/system for early warning.

analysis_limitations: static analysis only — no container run, no page-count instrumentation; the 1024-frame budget and the mechanism are exact, but the per-run dirty-page totals for 130 vs 72 columns are estimates
